source.title: Mini-batch Noise Lowers Sharpness via Dominant-Subspace Fluctuations

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own sharpness experiments, but does not test whether sharpness tracks a training–test generalization gap or measure generalization performance.
record.gate_note: The study measures top-k sharpness and training loss. Its results do not measure test error, a training–test gap, magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, or any other version's named outcome. Figure-only curves are described qualitatively in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures training loss and unscaled top-k Hessian sharpness, defined as the sum of the top-k eigenvalues. It reports no held-out performance or generalization gaps; Appendix D.2 explicitly states that all experiments use only the training split. Its sharpness results therefore do not test V7, and its batch-size comparisons do not test V5. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that dominant-subspace fluctuations induced by mini-batch noise help explain SGD's lower top-k sharpness, and adding their derived correction brings GD's sharpness evolution closer to SGD's. They do not demonstrate improved generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines top-k Hessian sharpness dynamics and a derived correction to GD; it does not reproduce the magnitude-aware perturbation measure or training–test-gap comparisons in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The sharpness trajectory changes with batch size; reversing the correction direction increases sharpness relative to GD. The reported experiments also vary architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Corrected GD nearly matches SGD's top-k sharpness trajectory for the MLP and substantially narrows the sharpness gap for the CNN and Transformer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A correction derived from dominant-subspace displacement covariance reproduces much of SGD's lower Hessian sharpness relative to GD.

fits_no_version.finding: Dominant-subspace noise lowers top-k sharpness whereas rank- and variance-matched random-subspace noise does not; training-loss trajectories remain nearly unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The subspace of injected fluctuations affects Hessian sharpness independently of substantial changes in training-loss reduction.

fits_no_version.finding: Dom-SGD lowers sharpness with little loss reduction; Bulk-SGD reduces loss similarly to SGD while maintaining higher sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dominant and bulk projected updates have different effects on training-loss reduction and Hessian sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing batch size moves SGD's sharpness trajectory toward GD's, and corrected GD follows that trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects top-k Hessian sharpness dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Reversing the correction increases sharpness relative to GD, while the original correction decreases it; loss curves remain largely unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The correction's effect on Hessian sharpness depends on its direction.

record.peer_reviewed: HiLD 2026: 4th Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: The experiments report training loss and top-k sharpness, not held-out performance or a training–test generalization gap. Results are mostly presented as figure curves and described qualitatively; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The derivation uses local approximations and assumptions, including frozen mini-batch noise variation.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were omitted. The plotted trajectory comparisons are recorded qualitatively because the text does not provide exact values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation='tests' conflicts with its otherwise correct T6 rationale. State changes to cannot_determine concern the supplied claim versions; they do not dispute the reported sharpness effects. Generalization statements in the related-work section and the final-accuracy statement in Section 2.1 describe cited work, not this study's results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural or random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and local-connectivity interventions.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its relationship to the training–test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and subsequent test accuracy.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer MLP with two width-200 hidden layers and tanh activation
rows.operation_detail: Compared mini-batch SGD, full-batch GD, and corrected GD using the derived sharpness correction.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k over training steps
rows.baseline: Full-batch GD reaches higher S_k than mini-batch SGD.
rows.value: Corrected GD almost overlaps with SGD in sharpness.
rows.note: The text describes the curves qualitatively; no test error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is accurate, but evaluates the proposed correction's sharpness trajectory, not any version's generalization outcome. Retain as fits_no_version evidence.

rows.subject: CNN on CIFAR10-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer CNN with width 32, ReLU activation, max pooling, and a linear classifier head
rows.operation_detail: Compared mini-batch SGD, full-batch GD, and corrected GD using the derived sharpness correction.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k over training steps
rows.baseline: Full-batch GD reaches higher S_k than mini-batch SGD.
rows.value: Corrected GD keeps S_k lower than GD and substantially reduces the sharpness gap with SGD.
rows.note: The text describes the curves qualitatively; no test error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: The reported reduction in the sharpness gap is accurate. Its incompleteness is not a partial observation of V7: neither magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance nor a training–test gap is measured.

rows.subject: Transformer on SST2-1k
rows.size_stated: 2-layer Transformer encoder with hidden dimension 64, 8 attention heads, ReLU activation, mean pooling, and a linear classifier head
rows.operation_detail: Compared mini-batch SGD, full-batch GD, and corrected GD using the derived sharpness correction.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k over training steps
rows.baseline: Full-batch GD reaches higher S_k than mini-batch SGD.
rows.value: Corrected GD keeps S_k lower than GD and substantially reduces the sharpness gap with SGD.
rows.note: The text describes the curves qualitatively; no test error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: The reported reduction in the sharpness gap is accurate, but the proposed correction's performance does not measure any claim version.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer MLP with two width-200 hidden layers and tanh activation
rows.operation_detail: Compared GD with mean-zero dominant-subspace perturbations and rank-matched random-subspace perturbations.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k and training loss
rows.baseline: GD and GD+Rand maintain high S_k; the three loss curves are nearly unchanged.
rows.value: GD+Dom maintains lower S_k than GD or GD+Rand while the loss curves remain nearly unchanged.
rows.note: The result concerns sharpness and training loss, not the training–test gap.
rows.check: Dominant perturbations lower Hessian sharpness with nearly unchanged training loss. Without held-out outcomes or magnitude-aware perturbation measurements, this cannot establish V7.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer MLP with two width-200 hidden layers and tanh activation
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD, Dom-SGD, and Bulk-SGD projected updates.
rows.measure: Training loss and top-k sharpness S_k
rows.value: Dom-SGD does not substantially reduce training loss but lowers S_k; Bulk-SGD reduces loss similarly to SGD but maintains higher S_k than SGD.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative comparisons; no generalization performance is reported.
rows.check: Figure 1 supports the stated projected-update comparisons, but training-loss reduction and Hessian sharpness do not measure any version's named generalization outcome.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer MLP with two width-200 hidden layers and tanh activation
rows.operation_detail: Compared mini-batch SGD at different batch sizes with full-batch GD and corrected GD.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k over training steps
rows.baseline: As batch size increases, the SGD S_k curve moves closer to full-batch GD.
rows.value: Corrected GD follows the same trend across batch sizes.
rows.note: Qualitative text description; no test error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: The MLP trend is accurately described, but compares sharpness over fixed training steps, not held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. It tests neither V5 nor V7.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST-5k
rows.size_stated: 3-layer MLP with two width-200 hidden layers and tanh activation
rows.operation_detail: Compared the derived correction with the same correction direction reversed.
rows.measure: Top-k sharpness S_k and training loss
rows.value: The derived correction lowers sharpness relative to GD; reversing its direction increases sharpness relative to GD, while loss curves remain largely unchanged.
rows.note: The text states the direction comparison qualitatively; no generalization performance is reported.
rows.check: Figure 6 supports the direction-specific sharpness result. This evaluates the correction mechanism without measuring generalization.
